correctness.rationale: For each private clique, parity forces either a positive odd root-color multiplicity and even base same-color degree (odd r), or zero root-color multiplicity and odd base same-color degree (even r). Labeled clique extensions are counted independently by r![z^r]sinh(z)cosh(z)^(q-1) or r![z^r]cosh(z)^(q-1). Gallai/Laplacian yields the sharp chromatic transfer, and consistency of Lx=d over GF(2) proves the exact odd-r two-color count. Direct tests independently inspect all 4,467,792 assigned colorings over 99 samples and binary boundaries over 1,099 labeled base graphs. Infinite conclusion rests on proof, not finite data.

value.rationale: The result gives all q-color counts (not only existence) for arbitrary base graphs under the widely used clique-corona operation. Odd-sized attachments collapse odd induced chromatic number to 1 or 2 and yield an exact GF(2) two-color count; even-sized attachments retain arbitrarily high base odd chromatic number or infeasibility. This produces unbounded, parity-controlled jumps on the known family of subdivided cliques and exposes a reusable local parity composition law.
